subject: Post-demo: FinWise fit notes, eval pack & model pin request
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@finwise.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@finwise.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 19:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Demo recap — quick follow-up

Thanks for the demo today, Jasmine — appreciate the walkthrough. A couple quick notes from our side: we ran a small holdout test overnight against our transaction classifier and saw an apparent drop in precision on merchant normalization after what looks like the most recent engine update you mentioned (around 2026-07-04). Before we go further, two asks: 

1) Can you share recommended model candidates (and a simple evaluation pack) so we can validate on our golden set?
2) If this is indeed caused by a model/version update, can Redwood pin us to the prior snapshot while we run the tests? We need to keep production traffic stable during that validation.

We’ll also share a short sample of failing cases (Alyssa will attach).

—Samir
FinWise — Head of ML


From: jasmine_liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir@finwise.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, tessa_morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 20:04:00 -0400
Subject: Post-demo: FinWise fit notes, eval pack & model pin request

Samir — thanks for the note and for bringing the failing cases. Helpful context. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps: 

Recap
- Today’s demo: ingestion patterns + merchant normalization pipeline. You outlined tolerance targets: precision >= 0.94, latency 95th <= 120ms for the normalization step.
- You reported a recent dip in precision starting after the July 4th runtime/weights deployment.

Recommendations (short list)- Candidate models to evaluate (fast to spin up via Redwood API):
  • rw-instruct-6b@2026-06-25 (recommended starting point — higher stability historically on tokenization-sensitive tasks)
  • rw-instruct-8b-q4a@2026-05-10 (lower-cost quantized variant; watch for edge-case hallucination)
  • community/bert-norm-probe-v2@2026-03-18 (for deterministic lookup-heavy cases)

Deliverables I’m attaching: benchmarking summary + an eval pack (prompt set + golden labels) so you can run locally: finwise_bench_report_20260711.pdf, finwise_prompt_set_v1.jsonl

Immediate ops proposal- To avoid customer impact while you validate, we can open an emergency pin request to freeze inference for your account to snapshot: rw-instruct-6b@2026-06-25 (this is the snapshot we saw stable in your test corpus last month). Pinning will route all production traffic to that snapshot until we confirm results or explicitly unpin.

Next steps- I’ll open the pin request now (internal SLA: 6 hours to confirm).
- Karhtik will prepare a short A/B plan and a quantization checklist so you can test cost/latency tradeoffs against your golden set.
- Can we do a follow-up call Tuesday 13 Jul at 10am ET to review results?

If you want the immediate rollback instead of a pin, let me know and we’ll treat as an escalation (longer internal approval).

Thanks — attaching the eval artifacts.

—Jasmine
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0172

Attachments: finwise_bench_report_20260711.pdf, finwise_prompt_set_v1.jsonl


From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>, Samir Rao <samir@finwise.com>
Cc: tessa_morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 02:16:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Post-demo: FinWise fit notes, eval pack & model pin request

Adding a few technical notes from the SE side — pulled from our internal checklist: 

Short diagnostics to run (local + on Redwood API)- 1) Run the provided prompt_set_v1.jsonl against rw-instruct-6b@2026-06-25 and rw-instruct-6b@2026-07-04 (the newer snapshot) and compare token-level diffs.- 2) Compute per-class precision/recall and confusion matrix; if merchant normalization drops are concentrated on long-tail vendors, we likely need tokenization/normalization fallback (community/bert-norm-probe can act as deterministic fallback).- 3) Run with KV cache warm and cold start — latency can mask as accuracy if timeouts cause truncation.

Operational notes- Pin vs rollback: pinning is reversible and immediate for your tenant — it doesn’t change the global model deployment, just routes your traffic to the snapshot. A full rollback (global) requires cross-team approvals and will take longer.
- If you want to test a cost-saving quantized path, try rw-instruct-8b-q4a@2026-05-10 behind a small shadow traffic run (10% traffic) for 24 hours. That will show whether quantization materially affects your precision.

I’ll prepare a short script you can run locally to produce the diff CSV and confusion matrices; Jasmine — I’ll drop that to the Drive link now.

—Karthik
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference


From: Samir Rao <samir@finwise.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa@finwise.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 09:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FinWise fit notes, eval pack & model pin request

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed. Alyssa confirmed the failing-case set is attached to her earlier message. Two things from our side: 

1) Please proceed with the emergency pin to rw-instruct-6b@2026-06-25 for our account. We want production consistent while we run the eval pack.
2) Karhtik — we’ll run the diff script as soon as you drop it and share metrics by EOD Monday. If the pinned snapshot preserves precision, we’ll schedule the A/B on the quantized variant for perf/cost tradeoffs.

Also, timeline question: how long will the pin remain active by default? We’ll need at least 72 hours to finish the golden-set runs.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Samir
